Claim 1 (Currently amended): A lamp comprised of an at least substantially hollow columnar body, a plurality of light emitting diodes disposed on said columnar body, a plurality of fins disposed on said columnar body, a base member disposed at a first end of the columnar body and providing a means for electrical connection, and an electronics module disposed within the columnar body and in electrical communication with the base member, wherein said fins are arranged in a non-uniform pattern relative to said diodes.

Claim 2 (Currently amended): The lamp of claim 1 wherein a second end of said columnar body is open.

Claim 5 (Currently amended): The lamp of claim 1 wherein said diodes are arranged in a non-uniform pattern radially around the columnar body.

Claim 6 (Currently amended): The lamp of claim 5 wherein said fins are arranged in a non-uniform pattern relative to said diodes.

Claim 11 (Currently amended): The lamp of claim 1 wherein said columnar body and said fins are comprised of a material having a thermal conductivity greater than 120 W/ mK.

Claim 14 (Currently amended): The lamp of claim 1 wherein said electronics module comprises a printed circuit board including circuitry for converting AC to DC current, and further including a thermal management system integrated within said electronics module. 

Claim 16 (Currently amended): A lamp comprising an elongated hollow polygonal body comprised of a material having a thermal conductivity greater than 120 W/ mK, a fin extending radially from each corner of said body, a light emitting diode mounted to each side of said body, a screw or wedge base connector closing a first end of said body, a second end of said body being open, an electronics module disposed within said body in electrical communication with said connector and said light emitting diodes, said lamp having a general A19 outline and further including a thermal management system integrated within said body. 

Claim 19 (Currently amended): The method of claim 17 wherein said body includes a plurality of integral radially extending fins, wherein said fins are arranged in a non-uniform pattern relative to said diodes. 

Claim 20 (Currently amended): The method of claim 20 wherein said body has substantially straight side walls, and wherein said body is extruded from a material having a thermal conductivity greater than 120 W/ mK.
